scope: Theorem 1 of the manuscript “A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction” (preprints/A-latest-anchor-induction-with-spectrally-compact-masks-for-worst-case-trace-reconstruction-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 122 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 56113d1f2019792b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For integer n ≥ 2 and 0 < p ≤ 1, worst-case trace reconstruction of binary strings is possible in this channel with at most exp O p−1 (log n)3 (1 + log log(2n))6  traces, with an absolute constant. Write q = 1 − p. More finely, when q > 0, setting X = 1 + log n/(1 + log(1/q)), the logarithm of the required sample budget is at most O p−1 (log n)X2 (1 + log X)6  with an absolute constant. In particular for fixed ε > 0 and 0 ≤ q ≤ n−ε the number of traces can be polynomial in n (with parameters of the polynomial allowed to depend on ε). The same asymptotic bounds also suffice for strings with general symbols (assuming exact observation of retained symbols).
